title: Understanding PowerShell Performance
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Understanding PowerShell Performance and define its core vocabulary.

content.intro: This lesson covers Understanding PowerShell Performance in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Measure a representative workload before optimizing. Reliable automation is modular, idempotent where practical, bounded in its retries and resources, and observable when failures occur. Avoid optimizing only for a synthetic benchmark that does not represent the real environment.

content_blocks.troubleshooting: Check command availability with Get-Command, inspect values with Get-Member, consult Get-Help -Full, and verify PowerShell version/platform before assuming identical output. Do not run examples that change system state without adapting and reviewing them.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.
